q1.name: What applications are Athlos X-ray sensors used for?
q1.answer: Athlos direct conversion X-ray sensors are used across three main application areas: dental imaging (intraoral, panoramic, and cephalometric), medical imaging (OPG, cephalometric, and custom medical modalities requiring high sensitivity at low dose), and industrial inspection (food & beverage foreign-object detection, pharmaceutical seal and fill inspection, oil & gas weld inspection, automotive casting inspection, PCB/SMT electronics inspection, and heavy-industry NDT and CT).

q2.name: Which Athlos product fits dental intraoral imaging?
q2.answer: The DC-Air® wireless intraoral sensor — Si-CMOS direct conversion, Bluetooth 5.0 wireless, Zero Profile® holders, up to 300 X-rays per battery charge, enhanced IP67 protection. FDA 510(k) cleared.

q3.name: Which Athlos product fits dental panoramic and cephalometric imaging?
q3.answer: The Ultra-Fast Scanning Sensor — an ultra-fast CdTe-CMOS direct conversion linear scanning sensor for dental panoramic and cephalometric imaging, as well as medical and industrial X-ray inspection. Single-photon sensitivity. Three models with selectable active widths.

q4.name: Which Athlos product fits industrial inline inspection?
q4.answer: The Industrial IP67 TDI — an IP67-rated ultra-fast TDI scanning detector for continuous inline inspection. No active cooling required. Used for food & beverage foreign-object detection, pharmaceutical fill/seal inspection, oil & gas weld inspection, automotive casting, PCB/SMT verification, and large-scale NDT.

q5.name: Why does direct conversion matter?
q5.answer: Conventional X-ray sensors convert X-rays to visible light via a scintillator, then detect the light. Each step introduces blur, signal loss, and energy waste. Direct conversion converts X-ray photons directly into electric charge, removing the scintillator step — yielding sharper images, higher contrast, wider dynamic range, and better low-dose performance.
